We discuss how cost engineering fits into the bigger picture as Lucid pushes forward in a competitive EV landscape.  

Whether you follow Lucid closely, are curious about their next moves, or just enjoy thoughtful conversations about the future of electric vehicles and autonomy, this one delivers real insight.

Lars Moravy on joining Tesla ⚡

“Back in 2009, I was at Honda—stable job, good life—but it felt uninspiring. I saw a ten-year roadmap of small engine improvements and realized this wasn’t the future.

Then I heard about Tesla’s Roadster project. It felt fast, real, and ambitious. A friend connected me with a recruiter, and after one call I started seriously thinking about it.

I’ve always loved cars and wanted to build something meaningful. Tesla gave me both. My wife was willing to move to California, so we said, let’s try it for a year.

That was 16 years ago… and I’m still here.”

Tesla is no longer just an automaker.

It’s building across the full stack of AI and robotics:

• Evaluation infrastructure
• Optimus humanoid robot
• Core software & code foundations
• FSD chip
• Dojo chip & Dojo training system
• Neural network development
• Autonomy algorithms

The goal is clear: unify hardware, software, and AI into one tightly integrated system for real-world autonomy.

Tesla is evolving into an AI and robotics company at scale.
